key_insight: When only synthetic speech is available, GRPO adapts an LLM-based ASR model much better than supervised fine-tuning, cutting WER far more effectively.
engineering_relevance: For privacy-constrained domains like banking, reinforcement learning on synthetic TTS data can outperform standard fine-tuning and deliver more usable ASR without collecting real speech.
method: Train on synthetic-only speech using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
Use a critic-free reward based on low word error rate (WER) hypotheses.
Optionally combine SFT first, then GRPO for the best final adaptation.
evidence_signal: On synthetic-only adaptation, GRPO reduced WER from 36.71% to 22.09% versus SFT, and SFT+GRPO improved the reduction to about 45% relative to the SFT baseline.
watch_item: The results are based on synthetic speech, so performance may depend on how closely the TTS distribution matches the target real-world audio.
paper_title: When Synthetic Speech Is All You Have: Better Call GRPO
